stem: Why can one product sample not prove a large drying load is uniform?
choices: One sample cannot establish uniformity across a large load because rack position, airflow, mass, and product variability can produce differences that require representative sampling.
One sample is sufficient if it is taken from the center of the room because central positions best represent average drying conditions.
Uniformity should be inferred from room-control settings rather than multiple product samples when the process is validated.
A single water-activity result can represent a cultivar lot because product from the same cultivar has equivalent moisture behavior.
rationale: A claim about a large drying load requires evidence that represents the load. Product state can vary with rack height, airflow, density, material mass, and local conditions, so one sample—even a valid one—describes only its sampled unit. Representative spatial sampling is needed when the decision concerns uniformity across the lot or room.
